title: The deployment is broken
summary: Restore a release by repointing the deployment symlink and verifying the service.

scenario.briefing: The current release symlink points at a release directory that no longer exists. The previous release is intact. Inspect the link, repoint it to the known-good release, restart, and verify.

objectives.description: Point current at the known-good release.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: Run readlink current and ls releases.
current points at 2026-10-20-skipped, which is missing.
The 2026-10-19 release is present and healthy.
ln -sf releases/2026-10-19 current; systemctl restart orders-api; curl http://localhost:8080/health.

misconceptions.description: Deleting the broken release path instead of restoring the link.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Deletes the current link or release directory instead of repointing current at a verified release.
misconceptions.feedback: The problem is the link target, not the old directory. Repoint current to a verified release.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a restart proves the deployment works.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Stops after restarting orders-api without requesting the health endpoint.
misconceptions.feedback: The service must start and answer a health request. A command exiting is not deployment success.

misconceptions.description: Believing deleting previous releases makes rollback easier.
misconceptions.feedback: Rollback needs an intact earlier release. Deleting previous releases removes the recovery target.

sections.title: Deployments are controlled state
sections.body: A common deployment pattern points a stable name such as current at a versioned release directory. Rolling back means changing that pointer to a known-good release. The old release must remain available during the switch.

sections.title: Recovery must be verified
sections.body: A symlink change is not a recovered service. After repointing, restart the process and check health. Keep the previous release until the new one proves healthy, so rollback stays possible.
